q2_gaps: Alphanumeric device/key designation ("F13"): the proper-noun rule enumerates people, places, organizations, works, vessels, treaties and named events, and a function-key label is a type-level designation (every keyboard has one) rather than a unique individual — nothing says whether it is a name-derived constant with a `Name` fact, a bare kind symbol, or a typed witness, and nothing says whether it needs a class atom.
notes: The multi-word name is correctly one opaque symbol with a single full-string `Name`; "press" takes `Theme` (the key is not created/destroyed/changed, and the unclear case defaults to Theme), and "can" on a specific subject correctly takes the event-level `(Can e)` rather than a kind-level `(can press)` property, with no tense atom beside it.
